# tests/fixtures/ — committed golden fixtures

Root of the oracle chain (`docs/design/cpu-backend.md` §6.1,
`docs/design/model-loading.md` §7): HuggingFace-generated fixtures validate
the scalar reference; the scalar reference validates everything else. These
are **committed artifacts** — CI and every dev build consume them from the
repo and never run Python. Regeneration is a dev-machine act via
`tools/regen_fixtures.sh` (see `tools/README.md`), reviewed like a code
change: a fixture diff means a generator or pinned-version change that must
be explained.

## Layout

```
models/
  tiny-llama/
    config.json                 # LlamaForCausalLM: 2 layers, hidden 64,
                                #   4 heads / 2 KV heads, vocab 512, bf16
    model.safetensors           # single-file form
    sharded/                    # SAME tensors, 2-shard form
      model.safetensors.index.json
      model-0000{1,2}-of-00002.safetensors
    expected/
      activations.safetensors   # fp32 forward goldens: input_ids (i32),
                                #   embeddings, layers.{0,1}, final_norm,
                                #   logits (all f32)
      meta.json                 # input ids, seed, generator versions
      ops.safetensors           # M5-T02: cpu::gemm goldens (per-case a/b/c
                                #   [+bias]); M5-T03: cpu::rmsnorm/softmax/
                                #   silu_mul/add goldens (rmsnorm_*/softmax_*/
                                #   silu_mul_*/add_* cases); M5-T04:
                                #   embedding_edge (bf16 embed table gather)
      ops_meta.json             # ops case manifest (cases + rmsnorm_cases +
                                #   softmax_cases + elementwise_cases +
                                #   embedding_cases; seed)
      rope.safetensors          # M5-T04: cpu::rope_apply / Rope goldens —
                                #   tiny_table cos/sin, tiny_sparse/tiny_contig
                                #   apply I/O, llama3 & linear scaled inv_freq
                                #   + cos/sin (docs/design/model-execution.md §7)
      rope_meta.json            # rope config params (tiny/llama3/linear; seed)
      attention.safetensors     # M5-T05: cpu::attention / Attention goldens —
                                #   per case x/positions/past_k/past_v/q_rot/
                                #   k_all/v_all/ctx/out (prefill empty, prefill
                                #   continue P>0, decode); GQA H=4/Hkv=2
                                #   (docs/design/model-execution.md §12)
      attention_meta.json       # attention case manifest (cases, dims, scale,
                                #   seed)
      # M5 adds more op-level goldens here (generate.json), each landing with
      # the ticket that consumes it — docs/design/model-execution.md §12.
  tiny-qwen2/                   # M5-T10: tiny Qwen2ForCausalLM (QKV biases);
                                #   same config/weights/expected/ shape
  qwen2-weight-names.json       # real Qwen2 checkpoint name/shape inventory
                                #   (no bytes) + the config fields the
                                #   weight-map tests need
  configs/                      # real, unmodified config.json files —
    llama3/  { config.json,     #   config-parser goldens (M4-T03); Llama
               LICENSE }        #   side is 3.1 for its rope_scaling block
    qwen2/   { config.json }
tokenizers/
  llama3/  { tokenizer.json, vectors.json, LICENSE }
  qwen2/   { tokenizer.json, vectors.json, LICENSE }
```

- **tiny-llama**: random weights (seed in `expected/meta.json`), generated by
  `tools/gen_fixtures/tiny_llama.py`. The activation goldens are the fp32
  forward pass of the bf16 checkpoint cast to fp32 — exactly what M5's scalar
  reference computes (convert-on-the-fly, fp32 accumulation).
- **tokenizer.json files are real and unmodified** — byte-copied from the
  pinned upstream revision, never re-serialized. Trimming vocabularies was
  considered and rejected (model-loading.md §7.1): merges and vocab are
  interdependent, and byte-identity against the real artifact is the point.
- **models/configs/** (`tools/gen_fixtures/model_configs.py`): real
  config.json files, byte-copied like the tokenizers. Llama is deliberately
  the **3.1** checkpoint — its `rope_scaling` block (`"rope_type": "llama3"`)
  exercises the presence side of the config parser, while the Qwen2 config
  exercises absence plus the omitted-`attention_bias` per-arch default.

## vectors.json conventions

Per case: `name`, the input (`text`, or `text_b64` — base64 of raw bytes —
when the input is not valid UTF-8, since JSON cannot carry it), `ids`
(`add_special_tokens=false`), `ids_with_special` (`=true`), `decoded`
(HF decode of `ids`, `skip_special_tokens=false`), and
`decoded_skip_special` (HF decode of `ids_with_special`,
`skip_special_tokens=true`).

Cases marked `"encode_synthetic": true` (the malformed-UTF-8 inputs) are the
one non-HF golden: HF `tokenizers` rejects non-UTF-8 input at its API
boundary, so these pin the *engine's* documented byte-fallback encode
semantics (model-loading.md §6.4) — each maximal invalid-byte run forms its
own pre-token, mapped through the GPT-2 byte alphabet and merged with the
real vocab/merges. Their `decoded` fields are true HF goldens.

## Size budget

Per model fixture ≤ **5 MB**; `tests/fixtures/` total ≤ **40 MB**
working-tree (model-loading.md §7.3). Current: ~16 MB, dominated by the two
as-shipped tokenizer.json files. Generators assert the per-model ceiling.
